arxiv-1804-11248.title: reductus : a stateless Python data-reduction service with a browser frontend
arxiv-1804-11248.creator: William, Paul
arxiv-1804-11248.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by William, Paul. The online data reduction service reductus transforms measurements in experimental science from laboratory coordinates into physically meaningful quantities with accurate estimation of uncertainties based on instrumental settings and properties. This reduction process is based on a few well-known transformations, but flexibility in the application of the transforms and algorithms supports flexibility in experiment design, supporting a broader range of measurements than a rigid reduction scheme for data.

arxiv-2110-10147.title: Parametrized tests of post-Newtonian theory using principal component analysis
arxiv-2110-10147.creator: Muhammed Saleem, Sayantani Datta, K. G. Arun, B. S. Sathyaprakash
arxiv-2110-10147.description: Abstract Searching for departures from general relativity (GR) in more than one post-Newtonian (PN) phasing coefficients, called a multi-parameter test, is known to be ineffective given the sensitivity of the present generation of gravitational-wave (GW) detectors. Strong degeneracies in the parameter space make the outcome of the test uninformative.

arxiv-2112-04867.title: RCSEDv2: Open-source web tools for visualization of imaging and spectral data
arxiv-2112-04867.creator: Vladislav Klochkov, Ivan Katkov, Igor Chilingarian, Kirill Grishin, Anastasia Kasparova, Vladimir Goradzhanov, Victoria Toptun, Evgenii Rubtsov, Sviatoslav Borisov
arxiv-2112-04867.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vladislav Klochkov, Ivan Katkov, Igor Chilingarian, Kirill Grishin, Anastasia Kasparova, Vladimir Goradzhanov, Victoria Toptun, Evgenii Rubtsov, Sviatoslav Borisov. We present a set of open-source web tools for visualization of spectral and imaging data, which we use in the second Reference Catalogue of Spectral Energy Distributions of galaxies RCSEDv2 (https://rcsed2.voxastro.org/). Using modern web frameworks Quasar and Vue.js we developed interactive viewers to visualize spectra and SEDs of galaxies and the diagrams presenting emission line ratios determined from the analysis of their spectra (BPT diagrams).

arxiv-2301-02852.title: Coherent control of wave beams via unidirectional evanescent modes excitation
arxiv-2301-02852.creator: Shuomin Zhong 1*, Xuchen Wang 2*, Sergei A. Tretyakov 3
arxiv-2301-02852.description: Abstract Conventional coherent absorption occurs only when two incident beams exhibit mirror symmetry with respect to the absorbing surface, i.e., the two beams have the same incident angles, phases, and amplitudes. In this work, we propose a more general metasurface paradigm for coherent perfect absorption, with impinging waves from arbitrary asymmetric directions.

arxiv-2505-21501.title: Vision Transformers with Self-Distilled Registers
arxiv-2505-21501.description: Abstract Vision Transformers (ViTs) have emerged as the dominant architecture for visual processing tasks, demonstrating excellent scalability with increased training data and model size. However, recent work has identified the emergence of artifact tokens in ViTs that are incongruous with local semantics. These anomalous tokens degrade ViT performance in tasks that require fine-grained localization or structural coherence.

arxiv-2507-10622.title: Spectral Feature Extraction for Robust Network Intrusion Detection Using MFCCs
arxiv-2507-10622.creator: HyeYoung Lee, Muhammad Nadeem, Pavel Tsoi
arxiv-2507-10622.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by HyeYoung Lee, Muhammad Nadeem, Pavel Tsoi. The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) networks has led to a surge in security vulnerabilities, emphasizing the critical need for robust anomaly detection and classification techniques. In this work, we propose a novel approach for identifying anomalies in IoT network traffic by leveraging the Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) and ResNet-18, a deep learning model known for its effectiveness in feature extraction and image-based tasks.

pmc-10739242.title: The Hombres Saludables Physical Activity Web-Based and Mobile Phone Intervention: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial With Latino Men
pmc-10739242.creator: Akilah J Dulin, Shira Dunsiger, Tanya Benitez, Britta Larsen, Bess H Marcus, Gregory Champion, Kim M Gans, Tiffany Leung, Eric Hekler, Scott Comulada
pmc-10739242.description: BackgroundOwing to structural-level, interpersonal-level, and individual-level barriers, Latino men have disproportionately high rates of physical inactivity and experience related chronic diseases. Despite these disparities, few physical activity (PA) interventions are culturally targeted for Latino men.ObjectiveThis study reported the feasibility and acceptability of Hombres Saludables PA intervention for Latino men.

pmc-11437158.title: Temporal dynamics of uncertainty and prediction error in musical improvisation across different periods
pmc-11437158.creator: Tatsuya Daikoku
pmc-11437158.description: Human improvisational acts contain an innate individuality, derived from one’s experiences based on epochal and cultural backgrounds. Musical improvisation, much like spontaneous speech, reveals intricate facets of the improviser’s state of mind and emotional character. However, the specific musical components that reveal such individuality remain largely unexplored.

pmc-11543976.title: Effect of Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Conditioned Pain Modulation in Trigeminal Neuralgia Patients
pmc-11543976.creator: Yu Zhang, Yiyuan Luo, Qixing Wu, Mingming Han, Haitao Wang, Fang Kang
pmc-11543976.description: IntroductionConditioned pain modulation (CPM) is a quantitative estimation of the capacity for endogenous pain modulation. Reduced CPM enables chronic painful event development or exacerbates pre-existing pain symptoms. Emerging reports indicate that patients with trigeminal neuralgia (TN) have dysregulated endogenous pain modulation. Transauricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is known to alleviate both acute and chronic pain symptoms.

pmc-12658909.title: Population Genomics and Connectivity of the Blue Mussel Species Complex: Insights From a North‐East Atlantic Hybrid Zone
pmc-12658909.creator: Eleonora Cariolato, Thomas Reed, Deirdre Brophy, Conor T Graham, Frances E Lucy, Luca Mirimin
pmc-12658909.description: Blue mussels (Mytilus spp.) are ecologically and economically important bivalves widespread in both hemispheres. Their relevance to coastal ecosystems and the aquaculture industry has made them extensively studied. The Mytilus complex consists of distinct genetic lineages, including Mytilus edulis , Mytilus galloprovincialis , Mytilus trossulus , and their fertile hybrids.

pmc-12720101.title: Enzymatic tailoring of anionic glycans for characterizing lectin and antibody specificities in a microarray format
pmc-12720101.creator: Lena Nuschy, Iain BH Wilson
pmc-12720101.description: Despite many studies on binding patterns of commercial lectins and other glycan binding proteins, unexpected recognition motifs are still revealed, highlighting the necessity to (re-)investigate these specificities deeply, as they are used for rapid screening of glycosylation patterns or diagnostic histochemistry.

pmc-12839137.title: Flexural Strength of Different Restorative Materials Used for Direct Restoration in Pediatric Dentistry: An In Vitro Study
pmc-12839137.creator: Ioana Elena Lile, Carolina Cojocariu, Ciprian Pasca, Andra-Alexandra Stăncioiu, Luminiţa Ligia Vaida, Diana Marian
pmc-12839137.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Preservation of tooth structure is a key principle in pediatric dentistry, where restorative materials must balance mechanical strength with the preservation of pulp vitality and minimally invasive techniques. The aim of this in vitro study, as it relates to pediatric dentistry, was to investigate the flexural strength of common composite resins, glass ionomer cements, and resin-modified glass ionomer cement within standardized and homogeneous laboratory conditions.

pmc-12866124.title: Clinical characteristics and factors associated with liver stiffness in patients with autoimmune liver disease: a cross-sectional study from the Kashgar region
pmc-12866124.creator: Palida Palahati, Maimaitiaili Tuerxun, Aziguli Abulaiti, Mireayi Tudi, Mayire Tuersun, Aikepaer Aiken
pmc-12866124.description: BackgroundAutoimmune liver diseases (AILD) are a heterogeneous group of chronic inflammatory conditions characterized by progressive hepatic fibrosis. While liver stiffness measurement (LSM) has emerged as a valuable non-invasive assessment tool, its clinical utility and associated factors in AILD populations remain incompletely characterized, particularly in understudied ethnic populations.

pmc-13631080.title: Dissociation between humoral and multi-omic immune responses to inactivated COVID-19 vaccination in patients with pulmonary tuberculosis
pmc-13631080.creator: Zhijie Jiang, Pengfei Jin, Xiaorui Nie, Jin Wei, Siyue Jia, Qiao Liu, Mingwei Wei, Xiaoyan Ding, Daming Zhou, Liguo Zhu, Limei Zhu, Mulong Du, Jingxin Li
pmc-13631080.description: IntroductionPatients with pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) may experience persistent immune dysregulation during anti-tuberculosis treatment, yet vaccine evaluation in this population has largely relied on humoral endpoints. Whether preserved antibody responses reflect coordinated systems-level immune activation after inactivated COVID-19 vaccination remains unclear. This study used systems vaccinology to identify multi-omic immune signatures induced by vaccination in PTB patients.
